paper_metadata.title: A 0.8-V 128-kb Four-Way Set-Associative Two-Level CMOS Cache Memory Using Two-Stage Wordline/Bitline-Oriented Tag-Compare (WLOTC/BLOTC) Scheme
paper_metadata.abstract: This paper reports a 0.8-V 128-kb four-way setassociative two-level CMOS cache memory using a novel two-stage paper, overcoming the drawback from the low gate-overdrive wordline/bitline-oriented tag-compare (WLOTC/BLOTC) and voltage, we describe a 0.8-V 128-kb four-way set-associative sense wordline/bitline (SWL/SBL) tag-sense amplifiers with an two-level CMOS cache memory using a novel two-stage eight-transistor (8-T) tag cell in Level 2 (L2) and a 10-T shrunk wordline/bitline-oriented tag-compare (WLOTC/BLOTC) and logic swing (SLS) memory cell with the ground/floating (G/F) sense wordline/bitline (SWL/SBL) tag sense amps with an 8-T data sense amplifier in Level 1 (L1) for high-speed operation for low-voltage low-power VLSI system applications. Owing to TC in level 2 and a 10-T shrunk logic swing (SLS) memory the reduced loading at the SWL in the new 11-T tag cell using cell with the ground/floating (G/F) data sense amp in level 1 for the WLOTC scheme, the 10-T SLS memory cell with G/F sense high-speed operation for low-voltage low-power VLSI system amplifier in L1, and the split comparison of the index signal in application. It will be shown that owing to the reduced loading the 8-T tag cells with SWL/SBL tag sense amplifiers in L2, this at the SWL in the new 11-T TC using the WLOTC scheme, the 0.8-V cache memory implemented in a 1.8-V 0.18m CMOS technology has a measured L1/L2 hit time of 11.6/20.5 ns at the 10-T SLS memory cell with G/F sense amp in L1, and the split average dissipation of 0.77 mW at 50 MHz. comparison of the index signal in the 8-T TCs with SWL/SBL tag sense amps in L2, this 0.8-V cache memory implemented
